name: Shoulder Dislocation - Acute Anterior
definition: Acute displacement of the humeral head from the glenoid, most commonly anterior, usually after trauma.

core: Pre- and post-reduction axillary nerve exam

investigations.principle: Imaging before/after reduction is selected according to trauma pattern and local protocol.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs confirm direction, reduction and associated fracture.

green: Short period of immobilization then rehabilitation
amber: Sedation, reduction technique and post-reduction management require clinical safety assessment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-sandhi dislocation phenotype may be documented only after modern reduction/stability care.

patientEducation.summary: Acute displacement of the humeral head from the glenoid, most commonly anterior, usually after trauma.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
